Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both 3D wake views—before touching the policy. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf under the required transfer protocol and record any actual source-to-policy transfer in the notes.

The workspace requires the visual-first skill as well as the bookshelf. I’ve confirmed the policy contract: only the candidate policy is editable in `solver/`, no CFD run is allowed here, and both provenance notes plus a durable guidance revision are mandatory. Next I’m comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure and checking their metrics/diagnostics against the images.

The evidence is unusually consistent: all four sampled policies self-propel on the same coherent alternating wake and capture on the same `23.4410T` sample. The best scalar variant only withdraws the slow route residual as the terminal stabilizer opens; it improves final distance by `0.00058L`, but terminal mean yaw/cross-track and peak moment worsen. A narrower progress-qualified handoff is effectively the baseline. That closes another scheduling branch, so I’m treating the remaining defect as carrier-versus-route signal separation, not a need for more authority or another threshold.

Bookshelf transfer is now informing the edit. I’m using the coupled-oscillator/averaging invariant that a rhythmic carrier needs both phase quadratures to be separated from a slow route signal. I’m translating that only as a bounded, normalized joint-angle quadrature added to the existing joint-rate carrier estimate; published CPG gains, clocked phases, species kinematics, and routes are excluded. The existing terminal yaw reference and posterior traveling wave stay untouched.

The notes are now written before the policy edit, including the required bookshelf block and falsification criteria. The candidate adds one mechanism only: a normalized angle quadrature in the slow main-route observer. Offline reconstruction cuts the beat-contaminated course-residual RMS by roughly 23% overall and 34% inside `3L`; the independently calibrated terminal residuals are deliberately unchanged.

The candidate, notes, and durable guidance lesson are all updated. I’m invoking the mandated lightweight check runner now; it will compare guidance semantically against the assigned parent, execute the policy contract with a synthetic state, and verify the solver boundary without running CFD.

The configured check-runner role could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this environment. I’m running the exact three commands from its TOML directly instead; these are the same non-CFD guidance, policy-contract, and boundary checks.

The guidance check passes. The policy execution check is blocked because this workspace image has no `julia` executable (the command fails before loading the candidate), so I’m substituting static schema/structure checks and still running the prescribed boundary validator.
I found a Julia module outside the default PATH, so I can complete the synthetic policy execution after all. I’m loading that module and rerunning the exact contract check now.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 candidate: a phase-complete slow-course observer using bounded joint-angle and joint-rate quadratures, restricted to the main route request.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [Evidence and bookshelf notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable control lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:194)

Validation passed for guidance materiality, solver boundary, and all 72 parameter references. The Julia smoke test could not execute because no Julia channel is installed and juliaup could not reach its download service. Formal CFD was not run, as required.
